The least-privilege documented capability is Read content, which covers reading page titles and content without write or administration capabilities.

findings.title: Public OAuth authorization flow with per-user token exchange
findings.detail: Public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 flow: the user is sent to the authorization URL, Notion redirects with a code, the app exchanges the code at the token endpoint using client credentials, and receives an access token and refresh token tied to that authorization.
findings.appliesWhen: Always for this app, because other customer workspaces will connect.

findings.title: Read content capability for reading shared page titles and content
findings.detail: Read content gives the connection read access to existing content. Without it, page, property and markdown reads return 403. It does not allow updates or page creation, which the request excludes.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to reading shared page titles and page content; boundary is the pages the customer shares, plus their children.

findings.title: Customer selects pages in the page picker; access is per authorizing user
findings.detail: The customer selects which pages to share in the page picker. Access extends to child pages of selected parents. Only pages the user has full access to appear. Only the authorizing user can interact with the connection in their workspace, so each user must authorize individually.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to every customer who connects; reads are limited to pages the customer selects.

steps.title: Send a test customer through the authorization URL and pick pages
steps.detail: Open the authorization URL from the Configuration tab in a browser signed into a representative test workspace. Approve access and select one test page in the page picker. The callback should return a code or an error parameter.
steps.doneWhen: Redirect to redirect_uri includes a code parameter, and the selected test page is shared with the integration.

steps.title: Exchange the callback code for an access token
steps.detail: Send the temporary code from the callback to the token endpoint using HTTP Basic authentication with client ID and secret. This is an unexecuted authorization step that produces the access token used by later reads.
steps.doneWhen: Token response contains access_token, refresh_token and workspace_id; the tokens are stored server-side.

evidence.quote: The body of the request contains the following JSON-encoded fields:
| `"grant_type"` | `string` | Always use `"authorization_code"`. | ✅ |
| `"access_token"` | `string` | An access token used to authorize requests to the Notion API. | ✅ |

fields: CODE_FROM_CALLBACK: code query parameter from redirect, single use
OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI: identical to authorization request value

steps.title: Read the title of a customer-shared test page
steps.detail: Retrieve one page the test customer shared, using the access token. Read properties.title to get the page title. A 404 means the page is not shared with this authorization.
steps.doneWhen: Response is 200 and the title text is returned from properties title plain_text. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

steps.title: Read the full markdown content of a shared test page
steps.detail: Retrieve the page as Notion-flavored markdown using markdown_version=v2. If truncated is true, call again for each returned unknown_block_ids value until none remain or each remaining ID returns object_not_found.
steps.doneWhen: Markdown is returned with truncated false, or every unknown block ID has been fetched or reported as inaccessible. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: Response JSON paths for GET /v1/pages/{page_id}/markdown: $.markdown (string)
When truncation or permissions cause unknown blocks, the `truncated` field is set to `true` and the `unknown_block_ids` array contains the affected block IDs.
The endpoint also accepts non-navigable block IDs returned in `unknown_block_ids` from a previous truncated response. Pass these IDs to fetch additional subtrees of a large page.

fields: PAGE_ID: same test page as title read

steps.title: Fetch a returned unknown block subtree
steps.detail: For each ID in unknown_block_ids from the truncated markdown response, request that ID through the same markdown endpoint. Treat object_not_found as inaccessible content and do not retry it indefinitely.
steps.doneWhen: Each unknown block ID returned 200 with its markdown, or returned object_not_found and is reported as inaccessible.
